quests.question: The recipe calls for both fresh basil ___ dried oregano.
quests.hint: The word 'both' at the start is already waiting for one specific partner word later in the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Both' always pairs with 'and' to add two items together as a matched set, never with a word built for choice or negation.

quests.question: Both the marketing team ___ the sales team attended the product launch.
quests.hint: 'Both' commits the sentence to exactly one matching partner word.
quests.explanation: Since 'both' already opened the sentence, only 'and' completes that fixed pair correctly, joining the two teams together.

quests.question: The museum offers both guided tours ___ self-paced audio guides.
quests.hint: Whatever follows 'both' has to be the one word built to complete that specific pair.
quests.explanation: 'Both' locks in 'and' as its only correct partner, showing that both options are genuinely available together.

quests.question: You can pay either by card ___ in cash at the counter.
quests.hint: The word 'either' is already signaling that only one of two options will actually happen.
quests.explanation: 'Either' always pairs with 'or' to present two genuine alternatives, never with a word meant for adding both together.

quests.question: Either the landlord fixes the heater this week ___ we're withholding rent.
quests.hint: 'Either' at the start commits this sentence to one specific matching word later on.
quests.explanation: 'Either' requires 'or' to complete its pair, presenting the rent decision as depending on one of two outcomes.

quests.question: The award goes to either the top scorer ___ the most improved player.
quests.hint: Only one of the two named players will actually receive the award.
quests.explanation: Since only one player can win, 'either' needs its matching word 'or' to lay out that single-choice pair correctly.

quests.question: Neither the printer ___ the scanner is working this morning.
quests.hint: 'Neither' has already set up a negative pair, and it needs its one matching negative word.
quests.explanation: 'Neither' always pairs with 'nor' to add a second negative fact to the first, never with a word meant for positive addition or choice.

quests.question: Neither the manager ___ his assistant could explain the sudden price change.
quests.hint: This sentence is stating that both people, together, failed to do something.
quests.explanation: 'Neither' locks in 'nor' as its required partner, showing that both people equally lacked an explanation.

quests.question: The film received neither critical praise ___ strong box office numbers.
quests.hint: The film missed out on two different things, both stated as failures.
quests.explanation: Two absent successes are being paired together here, which requires 'nor' to match the negative word 'neither'.

quests.question: The update not only fixed the bug ___ improved loading speed significantly.
quests.hint: 'Not only' is setting up a second, even more impressive fact to follow.
quests.explanation: 'Not only' pairs specifically with 'but also' to add a second, often more notable fact on top of the first.

quests.question: She is not only the lead designer ___ the main point of contact for clients.
quests.hint: Her role is being described as more than just the first thing mentioned.
quests.explanation: 'Not only' commits the sentence to 'but also', stacking a second responsibility on top of the first.

quests.question: The festival not only drew record crowds ___ raised more money than any previous year.
quests.hint: A second impressive achievement is being added on top of the first one.
quests.explanation: The sentence builds toward a second success stacked onto the first, which is exactly the role 'but also' plays after 'not only'.

quests.question: Whether you choose the window seat ___ the aisle, the flight time stays the same.
quests.hint: Two named seat options are being paired together, with neither changing the outcome.
quests.explanation: 'Whether' requires 'or' to present the two named alternatives, showing that either choice leads to the same result.

quests.question: The interviewer asked whether I preferred remote work ___ the office full-time.
quests.hint: Two work arrangements are being weighed against each other as named options.
quests.explanation: 'Whether' sets up two named alternatives that must be completed with 'or', matching the question's structure.

quests.question: Whether the client signs today ___ next week, the project timeline won't change.
quests.hint: Two possible timings are named, and neither one changes the plan.
quests.explanation: Two named timing options are paired here, and 'whether' always needs 'or' to complete that pair.

quests.question: ___ the coach nor the players expected such a difficult season.
quests.hint: The word 'nor' later in the sentence has already chosen its one required partner.
quests.explanation: 'Nor' only ever completes a pair that starts with 'neither', so that's the only word that can correctly open this sentence.

quests.question: ___ my manager or I will be available to sign off on the invoice.
quests.hint: This is a plain, practical statement about who can help, not an uncertain question.
quests.explanation: This is a straightforward statement of two people who can help, which pairs 'or' with 'either' rather than the more uncertainty-flavored 'whether'.

quests.question: ___ the practice test scores improve or they stay flat, the tutor plans to switch methods.
quests.hint: The plan stays the same no matter which of the two outcomes actually happens.
quests.explanation: The outcome doesn't depend on which possibility occurs, and that 'no matter which' sense is what 'whether' captures rather than a plain choice word.

quests.question: Both the deadline moved up ___ the budget got cut, which put extra pressure on the team.
quests.hint: Two full changes are being added together, not offered as alternatives.
quests.explanation: Two separate, complete changes are being combined here, and 'both' requires 'and' to add full clauses together just as it adds single words.

quests.question: Either the client approves the new design by Friday ___ the launch will slip to next quarter.
quests.hint: Two full outcomes are being set against each other, and only one will happen.
quests.explanation: Two whole possible outcomes are being weighed here, and 'either' still needs its fixed partner 'or', even across full clauses.

quests.question: Neither did the fire alarm go off ___ did anyone smell smoke, yet the whole building still evacuated.
quests.hint: Two full negative clauses are being linked, each with its verb flipped before the subject.
quests.explanation: Both clauses describe something that didn't happen, and 'neither' still requires 'nor' to join them, keeping the inverted verb order in both parts.

quests.question: ___ the manager or her assistant can approve the request.
quests.hint: This is a straightforward statement about who is able to help, not a question about doubt.
quests.explanation: This is a plain statement about which people can approve the request, so 'either' fits, rather than the uncertainty typically carried by 'whether'.

quests.question: I couldn't tell ___ the noise was thunder or fireworks.
quests.hint: This is about genuine uncertainty over which of two things was actually happening.
quests.explanation: Not being able to tell which of two things was true is a classic case for 'whether', which expresses that kind of uncertainty rather than a simple offered choice.

quests.question: ___ you arrive early or late, the door code stays the same.
quests.hint: The outcome doesn't shift no matter which of the two timings actually happens.
quests.explanation: The unchanged outcome regardless of the timing is exactly the 'no matter which' sense that 'whether' expresses.

quests.question: Not only did the flight get delayed, ___ our luggage also went missing.
quests.hint: A second, worse problem is being stacked on top of the first, matching the formal opening.
quests.explanation: This formal, inverted opening with 'not only' requires 'but' to introduce the second, even more frustrating fact.

quests.question: Not only does the app track your spending, ___ it also suggests a monthly budget.
quests.hint: A second, more advanced feature is being added on top of the one already mentioned.
quests.explanation: The formal 'not only' opening needs 'but' to introduce the second, more helpful feature that follows.

quests.question: Not only was the venue overbooked, ___ the caterer never showed up either.
quests.hint: A second failure is piling on top of the first, matching the formal structure at the start.
quests.explanation: The inverted 'not only' opening pairs with 'but' to add this second disappointing fact on top of the first.

quests.question: Both the CEO ___ the board voted in favor of the merger.
quests.hint: Two parties are being added together as both agreeing on the same outcome.
quests.explanation: Both the CEO and the board are being combined as agreeing parties, which is the fixed partnership 'both' has with 'and'.

quests.question: The tour is available whether you book online ___ in person.
quests.hint: Two booking methods are being named, and neither changes the tour's availability.
quests.explanation: The two named booking methods complete the 'whether... or' pair, showing both lead to the same available tour.

quests.question: Not only did rent increase sharply, ___ the number of available units also dropped citywide.
quests.hint: A second unwelcome change is piling on top of the first, matching the formal opening.
quests.explanation: The 'not only' opening requires 'but' to introduce this second, equally unwelcome development.
